title: How to Spend a Sunday in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Normal shops, supermarkets and chemists are shut all day on a Berlin Sunday** because of Germany's 1956 shop-closing law. The exceptions that save your day are station supermarkets, Spätis, restaurants, cafés, pharmacies on emergency duty, and museums.

**Start at a flea market.** Mauerpark in Prenzlauer Berg (about 9am to 6pm), Boxhagener Platz in Friedrichshain (10am to 6pm), Arkonaplatz (year-round) and the Nowkoelln Flowmarkt in Neukölln (first and third Sunday, April to November). Bring cash.
**Mauerpark is the Sunday centrepiece.** From roughly May to October, free open-air Bearpit Karaoke fills the stone amphitheatre from about 3pm, weather permitting.

**Sunday is a great museum day; Monday is the one to avoid.** Most Berlin museums, including Museum Island, run normal Sunday hours (the Pergamon stays closed for renovation). Book the big names online the night before.
**When the sun is out, go outside.** Tempelhofer Feld, the Landwehrkanal, Tiergarten and the lakes such as Strandbad Weißensee are the local Sunday. Buy your picnic first, because the shops are shut.
**Transport runs a normal Sunday timetable.** The U-Bahn only runs all night on Friday and Saturday, so check your last train on a Sunday night. Ferries count on a normal ticket.
